title: Jobs and their task lines
moduleTitle: App: Field service operations (proposed module; not in curriculum/structure yet)
audience: Owners and office staff who schedule, dispatch and record field jobs. No developer knowledge is needed.
learningOutcomes: Create a job with its customer, site and task lines.
Price each task line and explain where discounts are recorded.
Choose the right record change when a visit is cancelled.

instruction.heading: The job and its task lines
instruction.body: The job is the header for a customer request. Beneath it sit task lines, which are the concrete steps a worker must complete, such as remove old hinge, fit new hinge, test the door. Each task line can be ticked off, so the office sees progress without a phone call. Prices, unit amounts and discounts belong on the task lines too, not only on the header. That way the invoice can be built from the lines themselves.

instruction.heading: Cancellations and follow-up jobs
instruction.body: When a visit is cancelled, record the cancellation on the job. If the work still needs doing, open a follow-up job linked to the original. Do not reuse the original job, because then you lose the record of how often work is cancelled and why. Deleting a job also removes its linked visits, notes and task lines. Restore a deleted job only if the deletion was a mistake, because restoring brings the linked records back too.

procedure: Open a new job and attach the customer and the site.
Select the template, which fills in the default task lines.
Review the task lines and add any the template missed, one per concrete step.
Enter the price and any discount on each task line.
When a visit is cancelled, update the job status, and open a linked follow-up job if the work is still needed.

workedExamples.situation: A customer books a cabinet repair. The worker finds the cabinet needs replacing, and the customer agrees to a separate piece of work.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Do you add a task line to the existing job, or open a new job?
workedExamples.reasoning: The replacement is a different scope with its own price, so it becomes a new linked job. The original job is closed with a note explaining what happened.

equipmentAndPpe: A device with the Titan Zero Field app, where the lesson uses it

commonErrors.prevention: Price each task line so the total can be built from them.

commonErrors.error: Deleting a job to tidy up the list.
commonErrors.prevention: Close or cancel the job instead, so the history stays visible.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson covers app records and office process only. It does not grant, confirm or replace any licence, certificate or authority, and it makes no legal claim.

qualityStandard: Every job has a customer, a site and at least one task line.
Every task line has a price, even if the price is zero.
documentationEvidence: Task line list with completion ticks and prices
summary: A job holds the overall scope; task lines hold the steps and their prices.
A cancelled visit gets a recorded status and, if needed, a linked follow-up job.
Deleting removes linked records, so close a job rather than delete it.

knowledgeChecks.question: Where should a discount be recorded so that the invoice can be built from it?
A customer cancels a visit, but the work still needs doing later. What is the best record step?
options: Mark the original job cancelled and open a linked follow-up job
Delete the job and make a fresh unlinked one for the customer
Leave the job open with no status at all for the customer's file

knowledgeChecks.question: What does ticking off a task line tell the office?
options: That the worker has left the site
